profile.campus: Secaucus / North Bergen, Hudson County, New Jersey (Equinix New York metro campus)
profile.reading:
Equinix's own facility page places this building, NY4, at 755 Secaucus Road in Secaucus, New Jersey 07094, describing a two story, reinforced concrete structure of 151,771 square feet. Published specifications list N+1 power redundancy with 120v/208v distribution, N+1 UPS redundancy, N+1 generator redundancy with 30 or more hours of autonomy at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 5kVA, a floor load capacity of 150 psf, seismic design to Category B under the 2006 Universal Building Code, and a location above the 500 year base flood elevation. Security is listed as 24/7 with combination entrance mantraps, fire suppression uses a double interlock pre action system, and Equinix advertises a 99.9999 percent plus global uptime guarantee. Services on offer include colocation, Equinix Internet Exchange, metro connectivity, fiber cross connects, and the Equinix Fabric platform. No megawatt capacity figure and no year of construction are published on Equinix's own NY4 page.

NY4 is one of five Equinix buildings, NY2 through NY6, addressed within roughly a mile of each other around Secaucus in Hudson County. Data Center Frontier, a trade publication, reported in 2026 that Equinix's broader New York and New Jersey metro area totals nine IBX buildings and about 739,000 square feet of technical space, and it profiled one of those buildings, NY5, in some detail. NY5 was built in 2012 and expanded in 2016 to 20 megawatts of critical power capacity, fed by four utility lines and backed by eight 2.5 megawatt generators, with the campus staying online for a full week without grid power during Superstorm Sandy in 2012. That 20 megawatt figure describes NY5 specifically, a separate building from NY4, and Equinix's own NY4 page does not publish a comparable power number for this building. The same article described the wider campus as a hub for financial services matching engines used in stock exchange trading, without specifying whether NY4 itself performs that role.

Equinix, the operator, was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson and has grown into a global colocation and interconnection company running more than 260 IBX data centers across more than 70 metro areas, converting to a real estate investment trust in 2015. Its buildings function as carrier neutral meeting points where enterprise, financial, and media customers lease cages or cabinets and cross connect directly to network carriers and to cloud on ramps for AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and IBM Cloud. Hudson County's cluster of Equinix buildings, including this one, sits roughly ten miles from Lower Manhattan, a location shaped by cheaper New Jersey real estate and proximity to the Wall Street financial corridor rather than by any single anchor tenant.
profile.campus_sqft: Published individual square footage for four of the five Secaucus buildings totals 550,057 sq ft (NY2 131,040 + NY3 250,853 + NY4 151,771 + NY6 16,393 per Equinix's own site). NY5's individual square footage is not published by Equinix. The wider 9-site Equinix New York/New Jersey metro area totals roughly 739,000 sq ft of technical space per Data Center Frontier (2026).

The New Jersey facilities in this registry (Hudson County, Middlesex County, North Bergen, Secaucus) correspond to Equinix's Secaucus campus (NY2-NY6), while NY1 (the historic 165 Halsey Street carrier hotel in Newark, also tied to a Tishman operator record elsewhere in this registry) and other NY-branded buildings (NY7, NY9, NY11, and upstate NY13 in Elmsford) complete the 10-facility metro per Equinix's own site.

reading.body:
NY4 is a 151,771 square foot colocation building in Secaucus, New Jersey, part of Equinix's five-building campus in Hudson County. The operator publishes N+1 power and cooling redundancy and a minimum cabinet density of 5 kVA, but does not publish a megawatt capacity figure for this building. The neighboring NY5 building was reported to hold 20 megawatts of critical power as of 2016, but that figure describes only NY5, not this facility. At the published minimum density of 5 kVA per cabinet, this building's 151,771 square feet could theoretically accommodate roughly 600 racks at a typical deployment density, though the actual power supply to NY4 is not disclosed.

NY4 sits in a Hudson County cluster ten miles from Lower Manhattan, where Equinix operates five buildings within a mile of each other. The broader Equinix New York and New Jersey metro area spans nine buildings and approximately 739,000 square feet of technical space. Equinix describes its larger Secaucus campus, anchored by NY3, as serving financial, media, and enterprise customers with cloud on-ramps and exchange infrastructure. New Jersey as a state has 48 mapped data center facilities and only 5 with published megawatt figures totaling 111.3 MW, so NY4 represents one of the few facilities in its state where power capacity is disclosed.

Equinix's certification of N+1 redundancy across power, cooling, and UPS systems qualifies NY4 to host mission-critical enterprise and financial applications. The site was built above the 500-year flood elevation and designed to Category B seismic standards. No construction date or year of most recent expansion is published for NY4. The operator reports a global uptime guarantee of 99.9999 percent plus but does not quantify whether that applies to this specific building.
